title: What‘s the reason you switched to a paid AI Model?
author: BobOnTheBeach69
selftext:
I‘m still using the free ChatGPT model in the browser, not connected to the Engine or something. I don‘t really know what‘s the state of the art when it comes to AI but I feel like I should upgrade my setup.

So that‘s why I‘m asking what advantages there are when actually subscribing to an advanced AI Model like ChatGPT or Claude for example. 

Any suggestions what I should look into? I‘m using Unity Engine btw

comments.author: zenmatrix83
comments.body: autmated agent, mcp servers, computer use, and more that can't be done in the browser. its not the model its the tools you get for using something like codex and claude code

replies.author: Broskifromdakioski
replies.body: Hey can you give us some examples please on how your using mcp servers

replies.author: zenmatrix83
replies.body: look at the other comment there are blender unity and mcp servers as well. youtube has lots of examples

replies.author: BobOnTheBeach69
replies.body:
Is the automated agent actually capable of creating a prefab for example with some rules I give him? Could he automate the prefab creation for more complex objects like items and stuff? I always wondered what AI can do when I connect it to the engine.

Is the code that it produces even better with a paid model? I feel like my free model can‘t even handle a script with 1k lines sometimes. Does this get better with a paid model?

replies.author: No-Dot-6573
replies.body:
Yes to all. 
Dude you are living in the stone age of AI if you are still copy pasting from the browser.
It can even do all the configuration if you ask it to.

replies.author: BobOnTheBeach69
replies.body: 😂 yeah dude that‘s how I feel right now. I really want to upgrade. So this is all doable if I just use MCP server? Or what are the tools that I have to look into to achieve this? And would you suggest Claude or ChatGPT for this?

replies.author: No-Dot-6573
replies.body:
Yes, you basically need to have all programms you want the AI to use installed. Then get a Claude pro subscription and install Claude Desktop - it's simpler to beginn with. 
Start a new code session with Opus 5.5 and ask it to install all necessary mcps for your programms. (You could do it manually but that might be the first wow effect) Then completely restart the app (even in the tray, because MCP registration needs either a restarted or new session) 
Then describe what you want to create. Start small and see which workflow suits you. It is really easy. Claude should guide you all the way if additional things need to be configured (or configure it for you) like a good mentor until he is able to do the things you want him to do.
3d creation burns a lot of tokens, so if you connect Blender be warned that you are most likely going to switch to the max sub in no time.

replies.author: BobOnTheBeach69
replies.body: Do you have the 20$ subscription or do you habe max? I wonder if the 20$ subscription is enough when I just use it for Unity (I don‘t need it for other programs really)

replies.author: kytheon
replies.body: Don't be stupid. Get the $20 and see if it's enough for you. Don't jump to $100 immediately.

replies.author: No-Dot-6573
replies.body:
Just start with pro. If it isnt enough for you you can upgrade to max and just pay the difference. If you don't need it anymore you can cancel every time.
Since you asked: At work I have two Claude Max 20 subs and one chatgpt pro sub. 

For private use the claude pro plan and my local models are enough for me.

comments.author: slopgamedev
comments.body: for better code but now free models are better than what i paid for year ago. I think this will be last month i pay for this.

comments.author: OptimistDev
comments.body: I've had a max Claude and ChatGPT account for about as long as they've offered them because they're incredibly useful and I use them for tons of business and personal reasons. But because I'm now building a large-scale project. I'm currently using 100% of my usage on 3x Claude Max accounts + 1 ChatGPT Pro subscription.

replies.author: BobOnTheBeach69
replies.body: Damn what the hell are you working on

comments.author: shitty_advice_BDD
comments.body: Needed the coding and streamlining the asset creation.

replies.author: BobOnTheBeach69
replies.body: Can you elaborate on this? What does streamlining the asset creation mean?

replies.author: shitty_advice_BDD
replies.body:
Using something like Tripo, Meshy or Atlas allows you to take a drawing or whatever and turn it into a 3D asset and can even rig it for you so its basically game ready.

Like I was able to put Jason Voorhees in Bannerlord in about 30 minutes.

https://i.redd.it/hywo681oqayh1.jpeg

comments.author: Three_Tails_Studio
comments.body: Blender MCP, Unity MCP, Godot MCP, Unreal MCP, Git repository, cloud development. Basically pipelines.

comments.author: Fine_Comparison445
comments.body: If you're using AI mainly for coding, then I would strongly recommend Claude 5.5. Between GPT and Claude, I found it to be a better coding agent, and it also seems to last longer on a basic tier. Agentic AI, and frontier models are honestly night and day experiences and results compared to a free in-browser model.

replies.author: BobOnTheBeach69
replies.body: Yes I just use it for coding, I don‘t want to generate art with it. But I would love to try to connect it to the engine so it can automate prefab creation and stuff like that. It would be super cool if it would be aware of the scene and the hierarchy. Is Claude 5.5 also a good choice for that?

replies.author: Fine_Comparison445
replies.body: That is generally possible, but I think I would say it depends on what engine you're using. For example unity has an official plugin for agents. I have been using unreal engine personally and handle everything almost exclusively via code. I use vscode with a claude code extension.

replies.author: kytheon
replies.body:
Claude Projects is amazing, when it just spins off agents for small tasks.

But my favorite is having two projects talk to eachother. You can have one chat writing your code and another checking your code whenever it's done. Or one playtesting your game and logging bugs, while the other is specialized in fixing bugs.

comments.author: ralkuzu
comments.body:
ADHD

Claude be my door, my brain, my organizer

comments.author: heavy-minium
comments.body: Even if you use none of the extra features and use it like a caveman, there will always be one significant difference: the system prompt of the harness. For generic chatbot interface it's tuned to be general-purpose, while the coding agents (Codex, Claude Code, etc) have one tuned for siftware development.

comments.body:
Lmao, I couldn't go back to browser based workflows unless they take my cold dead body, I would rather program by hand (been doing it for over two decades).

Hope you can upgrade soon

replies.author: BobOnTheBeach69
replies.body: Lmao what is your current workflow? Do you use MCP too?

comments.author: kytheon
comments.body:
I tried ChatGPT pro for one month (it was free).

I made two entire new games and upgraded my two games in progress and wrote a bunch of tools. In one month I did more than in the past year. €0 well spent. then it ran out and charged me €20 the day before the subscription ended.

Now I'm still on that paid month. I'm convinced and might jump to the bigger plan..

I also got the €20 Claude sub. Claude Code is an absolute beast.   
You really don't know what you're missing for 20 bucks a month.

replies.body: Did you ever reach the token limit? And do you also use an MCP server to let the agent work in the engine? Or do you just code with it?

comments.body: I started with a Merlin in browser ai sub. Than opencode opened the world. Now I’m using Hermes telegram and have it working at home using a whole MacBook just for it.
